rv.q: The dialogue is zigzagging, joyfully absurd with the right amount of twists.
Bafflingly, it was a big hit in New York in 2014, but Blanche McIntyre’s production here is entertaining enough, despite an almost complete lack of sexual chemistry between the leads.

But Stage Kiss also has its sights set on the interplay between art and life – specifically whether onstage romance can conjure real feelings – and here it comes unstuck, thanks to some pointed but unsteady metatheatricality.

But beyond the comedy and the cast’s chemistry, Stage Kiss lacks a real sense of substance, and the storytelling falls apart slightly by the second act, which feels almost unnecessary in comparison to the tighter-paced first act.
Ultimately, it’s a silly comedy that comes off very old-school and uninspired.

cn.t: Ruhl's backstage romantic comedy about ex-lovers reunited on stage earns laughs but divides critics, with some finding it amusing yet lightweight and others praising its playful exploration of performance and intimacy.
